subject: Bulk erasure request + role clarification (Greenline Health)
messages:
From: Anya Sokol <anya@greenlinehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request for bulk erasure + role clarification

Hi Karthik,

We need Redwood's assistance to perform a bulk erasure for a set of user records tied to a decommissioned pilot. Attached is the formal request (greenline_dsr_request.pdf) with account IDs and timestamps.

Two quick clarifications before we proceed: 1) Under our current DPA, does Redwood act as a controller or a processor for the customer data stored/processed via the hosted API? 2) Can you provide an export of audit logs and a proposed timeline for erasure (we need to present this to our legal/compliance team)?

We'd like to limit user-visible disruption; preferable outcome is: export (CSV) of affected PII, verification by our team, then deletion. Please advise the verification steps you expect.

Thanks,
Anya
Privacy & Compliance Lead
Greenline Health
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-06-23T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Request for bulk erasure + role clarification

Naomi / Marissa — forwarding Greenline's DSR. They want: (a) confirmation of controller vs processor, (b) audit log export, (c) timeline for deletion. Attachment: greenline_dsr_request.pdf

Can you confirm the legal position and propose an ops plan (export + deletion) with ETA? I think we should: verify identity, produce an audit_log_export_sample.csv, hold retention on affected keys, then run deletion after customer's sign-off. Naomi — are SCCs / DPA amendments required here?

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-23T10:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request for bulk erasure + role clarification

Karthik — quick summary from a legal/privacy perspective:

- Role: For hosted API customers (including Greenline), Redwood is the data processor for customer-provided content per the standard DPA. The customer (Greenline) is the controller with respect to personal data in their account.
- Controller/processor nuance: We are controller only for aggregated, de-identified telemetry (see DPA §4.3). That does not apply to the requested erasure.
- SCCs: No immediate SCC amendment required for this DSR; existing DPA + SCCs (if applicable for EU transfers) remain sufficient.

Recommended steps (high-level):
1) Identity & scope confirmation: We require Greenline to confirm account IDs and provide a security contact by signing the acknowledgement in DocuSign (link below).
2) Export: Produce an audit-level export and an affected-records CSV (sample attached: audit_log_export_sample.csv) within 21 business days; shorter if ops prioritizes.
3) Verification: Greenline reviews export and confirms records to be erased.
4) Deletion: After verification, Redwood will schedule deletion and provide proof (deletion runbook and logs). Target: deletion to be completed within 30 calendar days of verification.

I will prepare a concise statement we can send to Greenline explaining role/limits. Also suggest we open PRIV-4321 to track technical work and evidence artifacts.

- Naomi
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-23T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request for bulk erasure + role clarification

Ops notes / suggested runbook (technical):

- Intake: We've got greenline_dsr_request.pdf attached. I will create an internal runbook entry (see redwood_deletion_runbook.pdf) and a ticket PRIV-4321.
- Retention hold: Immediately place a retention hold on the affected account keys to prevent downstream deletion/archival while we assemble the export.
- Export process: Scope the export to the requested time range and assets. We'll produce two artifacts: (1) per-record CSV with PII fields (encrypted in transit) and (2) audit log slice showing processing events. Sample: audit_log_export_sample.csv (attached). Ops ETA: initial export within 48 hours if we have identity confirmation; otherwise 5 business days.
- Deletion steps: After Greenline confirms which records to erase, we will: a) run dataset-level deletion job, b) flush KV caches, c) remove backups per our retention policy, d) provide deletion logs and proof of irrevocability. Estimated completion: 5-10 business days from signed-off export, subject to backup cycle.

I'll prepare the technical attachments and share a concise timeline for the customer.

-Marissa
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Anya Sokol <anya@greenlinehealth.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-23T14:30:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed plan: Greenline bulk erasure (summary & next steps)

Hi Anya — thanks for the request and for the details. Summary of our proposed mutual action plan: 

1) Role confirmation: Redwood is the processor for customer-provided content; Greenline remains the controller. We are also controller for aggregated telemetry only (not relevant to these records).
2) Identity verification: Please sign the acknowledgement we attached in DocuSign so we can proceed: https://www.docusign.com/eg/lease/agreements/0A12-DocuSign-link
3) Export: Ops will produce a scoped CSV export and audit-slice. ETA: 48 hours after identity confirmation (sooner if prioritized).
4) Review: Greenline reviews export and returns a signed confirmation of the exact records to delete.
5) Deletion: Redwood runs deletion job, flushes caches and backups per our runbook (redwood_deletion_runbook.pdf). Proof of deletion provided in logs. Target: final deletion within 10 business days of signed confirmation.

Attachments included: greenline_dsr_request.pdf, audit_log_export_sample.csv, redwood_deletion_runbook.pdf

Please confirm you can complete the DocuSign step today and whether Greenline's legal team needs any additional assurances (SCC references / DPA clause citations). Once confirmed, we'll kick off PRIV-4321.

Best,
Karthik
From: Anya Sokol <anya@greenlinehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Greenline Legal <privacy@greenlinehealth.com>
Date: 2026-06-25T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed plan: Greenline bulk erasure (summary & next steps)

Karthik / Naomi / Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround and concrete plan.

We can sign the DocuSign acknowledgement today. A couple of clarifications from our legal team: 1) Greenline will remain controller; we request the deletion proof include a hash of the deleted record set and the export manifest so we can verify completeness. 2) We want to retain aggregated analytics (non-PII) for internal product metrics — please confirm this will not be affected.

If you can confirm the manifest + hash approach and that aggregated telemetry will be untouched, we will complete the DocuSign step and expect the export within 48 hours.

Regards,
Anya
